title: The Little Kitten
lines: The kitten hops up on the table.
"Get off, kitten," said Meg. It sits still.
Meg sets it on the rug and pats it.
But the kitten hops back up on the table.
It bats a red apple off the table.
The apple bumps a candle and a bottle.
The bottle tips and spills on the rug.
The kitten hides in a red mitten.
Meg picks up the apple, candle and bottle.
She rubs the chin of the little kitten.
It naps in the mitten. Meg gets a rag.

questions.ask: What did Meg do the first time the kitten got on the table?
questions.listenFor: She set it on the rug and patted it — but the kitten hopped right back up on the table. Lines three to five.

questions.ask: What knocked the candle and the bottle over?
questions.listenFor: The apple, after the kitten batted it off the table. If they say "the kitten," ask them to follow the apple line by line.

questions.ask: Do you think the kitten meant to make a mess? Tell me why.
questions.listenFor: Either answer is correct. You want a reason — "no, it was just batting at the apple" or "yes, cats do that on purpose."
